learningObjectives: Understand relational database structures used in data analysis.
Construct basic SQL queries for filtering and aggregation.
Connect SQL operations to common data science workflows.

activities.title: Explore Database Anatomy
activities.instruction: Click the database components to reveal their roles.

content.concept: Relational databases organize information into tables containing rows, columns, keys, and relationships.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: A structured collection of related records.
A single record containing values for different columns.
A field that represents one attribute of the records.
A column or combination of columns that uniquely identifies a row.
A column that references a key in another table to represent a relationship.

activities.title: Build a SQL Query
activities.instruction: Assemble the SQL components needed to retrieve filtered data.

content.concept: A basic SQL query uses clauses such as SELECT, FROM, and WHERE to choose columns, specify a table, and filter records.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Sequence the SQL Analysis
activities.instruction: Arrange the stages of a typical SQL data analysis task.

content.concept: SQL analysis commonly involves identifying the required data, selecting and filtering records, aggregating results, and organizing the output.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Match SQL Operations
activities.instruction: Choose the purpose that best matches each SQL operation.

content.concept: SQL operations support selecting columns, filtering records, combining tables, grouping data, and calculating summaries.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: GROUP BY → Organize records into groups
JOIN → Combine related data from tables
